question.worked_solution:
The given parabola is written in standard form,

$$
y=a{x}^{2}+bx+c,
$$

with $a=1>0,$ $b=-6,$ and $c=10.$

Because the leading coefficient is positive, the parabola opens upward. Consequently, there is no maximum output, and the vertex corresponds to the minimum output.

The $x$-coordinate of the vertex is given by

$$
x=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac{(-6)}{2\cdot 1}=3.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=3$ back into the function to find the $y$-value of the vertex:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{2}-6x+10 \\  & =(3)^{2}-6(3)+10 \\  & =9-18+10 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertex is $(3,1),$ and the range of the function is $[1,\infty ),$ i.e. $1\le f(x)<\infty .$
